title: What Time-Based Art Archives Is
definition: Time-Based Art Archives: archives for art that changes over time.
description:
Time-Based Art Archives: archives for art that changes over time. This is Future Art, Design & Fashion at its most ambitious — time documentation research, archive logistics engineering and artist intent operations converging on a single goal: making archive hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Art, Design & Fashion will decide re-performance outcomes this century. Time-Based Art Archives is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working archive hulls, the larger time documentation vision stalls, and with it, the archive logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Time-Based Art Archives in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: Time-Based Art Archives
title: Real Research Today: Time-Based Art Archives
definition: Today's documented research behind Time-Based Art Archives.
description:
The road to Time-Based Art Archives is already being paved. Projection mapping festivals (Lyon Fête des Lumières) turn cities into canvases. Generative art (Refik Anadol, Sougwen Chung) fills museums with AI-driven works.

Algae-based textiles and dyes cut fashion's water and chemical footprint. Together these programs form the time documentation foundation that Time-Based Art Archives will build on — the archive logistics results, the artist intent methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as archive logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: Readiness Estimator: Time-Based Art Archives
definition: Estimates Time-Based Art Archives readiness from component maturity.

Honest scoring is the point: a archive hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Time-Based Art Archives operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Time-Based Art Archives installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 47845 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where time documentation monitoring, archive logistics redundancy, or artist intent maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Time-Based Art Archives Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Time-Based Art Archives: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Time-Based Art Archives — archives for art that changes over time.

Phase 1 — Prove (time documentation): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (archive logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (artist intent): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (re-performance): archive hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and museums-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
